A curated set of resources for the built environment, urban economics, and
teaching. I add to these lists as I find more. Students should start with the data
sources; most of them are free, and many can be downloaded at the census-tract or
metro level.

## Data sources {#sec-data}

### Real estate, housing & the economy

::: {.link-grid}
[[FRED]{.lc-title} [Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis — thousands of economic series, including rates, home prices, and metro data.]{.lc-desc}](https://fred.stlouisfed.org){.link-card}
[[data.census.gov]{.lc-title} [American Community Survey and decennial census tables down to the block group.]{.lc-desc}](https://data.census.gov){.link-card}
[[HUD User datasets]{.lc-title} [Fair Market Rents, income limits, CHAS affordability data, and LIHTC properties.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.huduser.gov/portal/pdrdatas_landing.html){.link-card}
[[FHFA House Price Index]{.lc-title} [Repeat-sales home price indexes for the nation, states, metros, counties, and ZIP codes.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.fhfa.gov/data/hpi){.link-card}
[[Zillow Research data]{.lc-title} [Home value (ZHVI) and rent (ZORI) indexes, inventory, and sales data.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.zillow.com/research/data/){.link-card}
[[Census building permits]{.lc-title} [Monthly and annual new residential construction permits by metro and place.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.census.gov/construction/bps/){.link-card}
[[Bureau of Labor Statistics]{.lc-title} [Employment, wages, CPI, and construction-cost data.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.bls.gov){.link-card}
[[BEA regional data]{.lc-title} [GDP and personal income by state, county, and metro area.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.bea.gov/data/by-place-county-metro-local){.link-card}
[[NCREIF]{.lc-title} [The NCREIF Property Index and other institutional real estate performance benchmarks.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.ncreif.org){.link-card}
[[Nareit data & research]{.lc-title} [REIT index returns, market capitalization, and sector data.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.reit.com/data-research){.link-card}
[[NLIHC — Out of Reach]{.lc-title} [The housing wage needed to afford a modest rental in every state, metro, and county.]{.lc-desc}](https://nlihc.org/oor){.link-card}
[[Eviction Lab]{.lc-title} [Eviction filing data and tracking for U.S. cities and states (Princeton).]{.lc-desc}](https://evictionlab.org){.link-card}
:::

### Spatial, urban & transportation

::: {.link-grid}
[[IPUMS]{.lc-title} [Harmonized census and survey microdata (USA, CPS, international).]{.lc-desc}](https://www.ipums.org){.link-card}
[[NHGIS]{.lc-title} [Historical census tables and GIS boundary files from 1790 to the present.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.nhgis.org){.link-card}
[[Census TIGER/Line]{.lc-title} [Shapefiles for tracts, block groups, roads, and places.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/tiger-line-file.html){.link-card}
[[LEHD / LODES]{.lc-title} [Where people live and work: block-level origin–destination employment data.]{.lc-desc}](https://lehd.ces.census.gov){.link-card}
[[EPA Smart Location Database]{.lc-title} [Density, land-use diversity, street design, and transit access for every block group.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.epa.gov/smartgrowth/smart-location-mapping){.link-card}
[[National Zoning Atlas]{.lc-title} [Standardized, mappable zoning codes across U.S. jurisdictions.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.zoningatlas.org){.link-card}
[[Urban Institute Data Catalog]{.lc-title} [Datasets from Urban's housing, finance, and neighborhood research.]{.lc-desc}](https://datacatalog.urban.org){.link-card}
:::

### Climate, energy & environment

::: {.link-grid}
[[NOAA NCEI]{.lc-title} [Historical climate and weather data, including temperature and precipitation records.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov){.link-card}
[[Climate Mapping for Resilience & Adaptation]{.lc-title} [County-level projections of heat, drought, flooding, and wildfire.]{.lc-desc}](https://resilience.climate.gov){.link-card}
[[ENERGY STAR benchmarking]{.lc-title} [Portfolio Manager, the standard tool for measuring building energy and water use.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.energystar.gov/buildings/benchmark){.link-card}
[[USGBC project directory]{.lc-title} [Searchable directory of LEED-certified projects and their scorecards.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.usgbc.org/projects){.link-card}
:::

::: {.link-grid}
[[Denver Open Data Catalog]{.lc-title} [City and County of Denver datasets: parcels, zoning, permits, and more.]{.lc-desc}](https://opendata-geospatialdenver.hub.arcgis.com/){.link-card}
[[Colorado Information Marketplace]{.lc-title} [The State of Colorado's open data portal.]{.lc-desc}](https://data.colorado.gov){.link-card}
[[DRCOG Regional Data Catalog]{.lc-title} [Denver Regional Council of Governments data on land use, transportation, and growth.]{.lc-desc}](https://data.drcog.org){.link-card}
[[State Demography Office]{.lc-title} [Colorado population estimates and forecasts by county and municipality.]{.lc-desc}](https://demography.dola.colorado.gov){.link-card}

## Sustainability & regenerative development {#sec-environmental}

A collection of resources about the environment, with a particular focus on the
built environment, for students and researchers interested in regenerative
solutions to city building, transportation, and other built-environment problems.

::: {.link-grid}
[[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]{.lc-title} [The IPCC's assessment reports on the science of climate change.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.ipcc.ch){.link-card}
[[*A Green New Deal* (2008)]{.lc-title} [New Economics Foundation's original Green New Deal report (archived).]{.lc-desc}](https://web.archive.org/web/20081010184615/http://www.neweconomics.org:80/gen/uploads/2ajogu45c1id4w55tofmpy5520072008172656.pdf){.link-card}
[[Regenesis Group]{.lc-title} [Pioneers of regenerative development and design practice.]{.lc-desc}](https://regenesisgroup.com){.link-card}
[[International Living Future Institute]{.lc-title} [Home of the Living Building Challenge.]{.lc-desc}](https://living-future.org){.link-card}
[[U.S. Green Building Council]{.lc-title} [The LEED rating system and green-building education.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.usgbc.org){.link-card}
[[Capital Institute]{.lc-title} [Regenerative economics and the principles of a regenerative economy.]{.lc-desc}](https://capitalinstitute.org){.link-card}
[[Doughnut Economics Action Lab]{.lc-title} [Tools for cities applying Kate Raworth's doughnut framework.]{.lc-desc}](https://doughnuteconomics.org){.link-card}
[[CityCraft Foundation]{.lc-title} [Regenerative city-building in West Denver and beyond.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.citycraftfoundation.org){.link-card}
:::

**Resiliency frameworks**

::: {.link-grid}
[[Resilient Cities Network]{.lc-title} [The successor network to the Rockefeller Foundation's 100 Resilient Cities.]{.lc-desc}](https://resilientcitiesnetwork.org){.link-card}
[[UN SDGs — 2019 U.S. Cities Report]{.lc-title} [How the 100 largest U.S. metros perform on the Sustainable Development Goals.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.sustainabledevelopment.report/reports/2019-us-cities-sustainable-development-report/){.link-card}
[[Colorado Resiliency Office]{.lc-title} [State resources for community resilience planning.]{.lc-desc}](https://coresiliency.colorado.gov/){.link-card}
:::

## Discussion-based teaching {#sec-discussion}

I use discussion in my topics class, *Triple Bottom Line and the Built
Environment*, to encourage students to engage deeply with material on social
justice and environmental sustainability — including by facilitating their own
class discussions. As Brookfield and Preskill describe it, the purposes of
discussion are fourfold: (1) to help participants reach a more critically
informed understanding of the topic, (2) to enhance their self-awareness and
capacity for self-critique, (3) to foster an appreciation for the diversity of
opinion that emerges when viewpoints are exchanged openly and honestly, and
(4) to act as a catalyst for taking informed action in the world.

::: {.link-grid}
[[Stephen Brookfield's website]{.lc-title} [Works, resources, and tools for facilitating discussion and adult learning, including the Critical Incident Questionnaire.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.stephenbrookfield.com){.link-card}
[[DU Office of Teaching and Learning]{.lc-title} [Resources for teaching and for using technology to support learning.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.du.edu/otl){.link-card}
[[*The Discussion Book: 50 Great Ways to Get People Talking*]{.lc-title} [A one-page summary of the book's 50 methods (Columbia CTL).]{.lc-desc}](https://ctl.columbia.edu/files/2017/02/2017.02.15.teacherslounge-50waystoholddiscussion-1y0tber.pdf){.link-card}
:::

> Brookfield, S. D., & Preskill, S. (2005). *Discussion as a Way of Teaching:
> Tools and Techniques for Democratic Classrooms.* John Wiley & Sons.

## Technology in the classroom {#sec-technology}

I like to use technology in the classroom to give students the opportunity to
share their work with the world. A few tools I point them to:

**Website hosting**

- [WordPress](https://wordpress.com), [Weebly](https://www.weebly.com), [Wix](https://www.wix.com), [Adobe Portfolio](https://portfolio.adobe.com), and DU Portfolio

**Infographics & visualization**

::: {.link-grid}
[[Kumu]{.lc-title} [For creating complex network story maps.]{.lc-desc}](https://kumu.io){.link-card}
[[Canva]{.lc-title} [For visual editing and layout.]{.lc-desc}](https://www.canva.com){.link-card}
:::
